name: recordDate
description: Date (and, optionally, time) that peat depth measurement was taken, typically in format YYYY-MM-DD.

name: surveyor
description: Name or names of persons, groups, or organisations who recorded the peat depth measurement. Note that personal data must be managed in accordance with the principles of the Data Protection Act 2018 [6] and/or any subsequent legal provisions.

name: institution
description: The name (or acronym) in use by the institution having custody of the particular record. Full names are recommended to avoid potential ambiguities.

name: location
description: Spatial region or named place.

name: country
description: Country or major administrative unit in which the Location occurs.

name: latitude
requirement_text: Required if gridReference, and easting and northing, not provided
description: The geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic centre from where the measurement was taken.

name: longitude
requirement_text: Required if gridReference, and easting and northing, not provided
description: The geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic centre from where the measurement was taken.

name: coordinateUncertainty
requirement_text: Desirable if latitude and longitude provided
description: The horizontal distance, i.e. radius, (in metres) from the given latitude and longitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the record location. This can allow for GPS inaccuracy. Leave the value empty if the uncertainty is unknown and cannot be estimated, or is not applicable (because there are no coordinates).

name: geodeticDatum
requirement_text: Required if latitude and longitude provided
description: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in latitude and longitude are based. Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the SRS, if known (e.g. EPSG:4326 for WGS 84).

name: gridReference
requirement_text: Required if latitude and longitude, and easting and northing, not provided
description: Location of the record using the Ordnance Survey National Grid reference system [footnote 2]. Recommended precision is for at least eight-figure grid references, i.e. 10m x 10m.

name: easting
dwc_note: Component of verbatimCoordinates. For Darwin Core export, combine as "<easting> <northing>" and give the reference system in verbatimSRS.
requirement_text: Required if latitude and longitude, and gridReference, not provided
description: Easting of the record, in metres, using OSGB36 National Grid, or the projected reference system given in verbatimSRS.

name: northing
dwc_note: Component of verbatimCoordinates. For Darwin Core export, combine as "<easting> <northing>" and give the reference system in verbatimSRS.
requirement_text: Required if latitude and longitude, and gridReference, not provided
description: Northing of the record, in metres, using OSGB36 National Grid, or the projected reference system given in verbatimSRS.

name: verbatimSRS
requirement_text: Desirable if easting and northing provided; if absent, EPSG:27700 is assumed
description: The spatial reference system (SRS) of easting and northing. Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code, e.g. EPSG:27700 for British National Grid, or EPSG:25833 for ETRS89 / UTM zone 33N.

name: locationRemarks
description: Comments or notes about the specific location of this measurement. Particular surveys may consider use of the IUCN Peatland Code [8] Condition Category for this, e.g. "Near Natural", "Modified"

name: surfacePeatDepth
description: Maximum depth of surface peat (organic soil depth), measured from the surface, specified in centimetres. Depth may be zero if there is no surface peat.

name: peatDepthResolution
description: The description of the potential error, if any, associated with the surfacePeatDepth measurement, e.g. was peat depth measured to the nearest 1cm, or 10cm, or was the bottom difficult to ascertain with certainty? peatDepthRemarks should be used to provide further details, including any difference with resolution for buried peat measurements.

name: peatPresence
description: Alternative to surfacePeatDepth, providing a simple indication of whether peat was present at the location. The peatDepthRemarks attribute may be used for further detail, e.g. "Visual check".

name: buriedPeatStartDepth
description: Start point of buried peat layer from the surface, i.e. depth first detected, specified in centimetres.

name: buriedPeatEndDepth
description: End point of buried peat layer from the surface, i.e. maximum depth, specified in centimetres.

name: surfaceElevation
dwc_note: Stored in centimetres. For Darwin Core export, divide by 100 and write the same value to both minimumElevationInMeters and maximumElevationInMeters; the reference level goes in verticalDatum.
description: Elevation of the ground surface, specified in centimetres, above the reference level given in verticalDatum. Useful in areas such as degrading or eroding peatlands, where elevation could change over time.

name: verticalDatum
description: The vertical datum (reference level) upon which surfaceElevation is based. Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the vertical reference system, e.g. EPSG:5701 for Ordnance Datum Newlyn or EPSG:5941 for NN2000 (Norway). For heights relative to a local benchmark, describe the benchmark here.

name: probeType
allowed_values: peat probe|avalanche probe|cable rod|drainage rod|threaded rod|peat borer|soil corer|open end corer|stick|other
description: Type of peat probe or other sampling method. The "other" option may be used for devices used that are not actually peat probes, e.g. surface level rods, supported by peatDepthRemarks for additional details.

name: probeReachedBottom
description: Was the base of the peat layer(s) reached, e.g. was probe long enough to measure the full depth of peat? As opposed to suspecting that peat continued to lower depths that could not be measured. "No" means that the full depth of peat was not measured, and hence the surfacePeatDepth recorded is a minimum value only. "No" should also be used if the surveyor was unsure.

name: peatDepthRemarks
description: Comments or notes on this peat depth measurement. Can include an assessment of confidence, e.g. if it is difficult to determine the exact bottom of the organic layer, density of substrate preventing recording a deeper depth using peat probes etc.
